images.title: When is the HCF the multiplier?
images.purpose: Recap the test: the HCF equals the common multiplier only when the other two factors are co-prime.
images.composition: Two equal panels side by side with a thin grey divider and generous margins, each holding three short lines.
exact_structure: Left panel, green #009E73 border, 3 lines: 6 × 4 and 6 × 5, then 4, 5 co-prime, then HCF = 6.
Right panel, amber #E69F00 border, 3 lines: 6 × 4 and 6 × 10, then 4, 10 share 2, then HCF = 6 × 2 = 12.
In both panels the common multiplier 6 in the first line is drawn in teal #0072B2.
One thin grey #6B7280 vertical divider between the two panels.
rejection: a left HCF other than 6 or a right HCF other than 12
images.takeaway: Check the other factors: if they are co-prime the HCF is the multiplier, otherwise it is the multiplier times their HCF.
images.description: Two panels: 6 × 4 and 6 × 5 with HCF 6, and 6 × 4 and 6 × 10 with HCF 6 × 2 = 12.
images.context: Shown beside the practice on common multipliers and the HCF.
images.teaching_notes: For each practice pair, cover the multiplier and ask whether the leftover factors share anything.

image_decisions.why: A two case recap gives students a quick test to apply in the practice.
